Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Designing Workflows for Co-Intelligence—Practical Integration Strategies.
Now that you’ve got a clear sense of what humans and AI each bring to the table, the next step is figuring out how to actually blend those strengths into your day-to-day work.
And here’s the thing—it’s not about flipping your whole process upside down. It’s more about weaving AI in, so it fits naturally and feels genuinely helpful, not forced.
Think of it like a rhythm: AI jumps in where it’s great at crunching numbers, generating ideas, or suggesting options, and then you—or your team—step in to add context, make decisions, and give everything that human touch.
Let’s look at a practical way to do this.
Start by mapping out the steps of a typical task or project. Where could AI really make a difference?
For example, in a product development cycle, you might have AI quickly scan market trends—digging through massive datasets to spot new patterns or customer needs you might otherwise miss.
Then, maybe it jumps in to suggest some fresh design ideas or features, building on what’s already out there.
It could even draft the first version of user manuals, FAQs, or marketing copy, so your team isn’t starting from scratch.
But here’s where the magic happens: at every stage, it’s the human team members who review, refine, and make those big decisions.
You can picture this like a relay race—the baton moving back and forth between AI and people. Each takes the lead when their strengths matter most.
To keep things running smoothly, there are a few things that really help:
First, define clear roles. Spell out which steps are a good fit for AI, and which need a human touch.
Next, set up checkpoints. Build in moments to pause, review, and adjust course if needed.
And don’t forget to document what you learn. Keep track of what’s working, and what isn’t, so you can keep improving your process.
Here’s a real-world example: look at customer service.
Lots of companies now use AI chatbots to handle routine questions—like order tracking or password resets. That frees up human agents to focus on the tougher, more sensitive stuff, where empathy and good judgment make all the difference.
In this kind of workflow, the AI takes care of triaging requests, but as soon as something needs a personal touch, a human takes over.
The key is, this isn’t a set-it-and-forget-it situation. As AI gets better and your team’s needs change, you’ll want to revisit and tweak your workflows.
Teams that make a habit of refining how they work with AI are the ones that will adapt fastest—and really thrive as things evolve.
